summary: Facepalm: Facepalm scan for 2026-10-02 (window 2026-09-26 to 2026-10-02). No candidate met every rule, so this run submits none. The search tool hit its usage limit partway through. Most election-blunder stories it surfaced were first reported after the scan date: Maricopa County, Colorado's passenger-rail ballot question, Calaveras County, Oxford County in Maine, Athens-Clarke County, Pender County and Kendall County. The few stories inside the window had no coverage from accepted publishers, or I couldn't open the pages. The Maryland sign story from the earlier scan logs was checked again, but the page couldn't be opened. Stories from earlier scan logs that were already set aside were not proposed again without new facts. Genius: Genius scan for 2026-10-02 (window Sept 26 to Oct 2). The search and fetch tool limits ran out partway through the scan, so many leads could only be checked against one page. Only one candidate cleared the two-source rule: NC State's Plant Armor fabric cover, which raised strawberry yields up to 3.56 times. NC State announced it on Sept 29; the sources are the university release and ScienceDaily (Oct 1). One date issue: the journal Agriculture published the paper on Sept 25, one day before the window. The candidate is dated to the announcement, and the summary says so. Other leads were set aside because they had only one accepted source, came out too early or too late, or were led from outside the US. No genius or facepalm story met the standard; nothing published.

candidates.headline: NC State fabric cover raises strawberry yields up to 3.56 times in tunnel field tests
candidates.reason: fails the schema: ✖ summary is longer than three sentences

candidates.headline: Some Michigan voters, including in Antrim and Presque Isle counties, still lack absentee ballots after clerks miss the state mailing deadline
candidates.reason: In the date window (Sept 29–30, 2026), but the only coverage found was Votebeat, Michigan Advance, Interlochen Public Radio, Hoodline and syndicated radio sites. None of them is on the accepted list, and search capacity ran out before I could find an accepted second source.

candidates.headline: Antrim County, Mich., clerk faces recall effort after the state removed her voter-file access
candidates.reason: Michigan Public (Sept 30) is accepted, but the story centers on contested allegations and a recall campaign, not a clear self-evident blunder, and it has a partisan election-administration angle. I found no second accepted source.

candidates.headline: About 800,000 Colorado voters get ballots wrongly including the Front Range Passenger Rail tax question
candidates.reason: Reported Oct 7, 2026 (CPR, Gazette, 9News), which is after the scan date.

candidates.headline: Pender County, N.C., sends incorrect property tax bills
candidates.reason: Reported Oct 6, 2026, after the scan date, and the source found (Port City Daily) isn't on the accepted list.

candidates.headline: Maine says a packaging error sent wrong ballots to some Oxford County voters
candidates.reason: Reported Oct 7–8, 2026 (Press Herald), after the scan date.

candidates.headline: Toledo repaves a street after the city says the first attempt did not meet quality standards
candidates.reason: Reported Sept 22, 2026, before the 7-day window; only one accepted source found (13abc).

candidates.headline: Maryland city fixes a sign misspelled for 20 years
candidates.reason: Appears to have been reported around Oct 4, after the scan date. The Tucson.com AP republication couldn't be opened to confirm the date.

candidates.headline: SpaceX Crew-13 docks at the ISS 7 hours 55 minutes after launch, the fastest trip by a US spacecraft (Oct. 1, FL)
candidates.reason: Only one accepted source was opened (Space.com); the other page found was SpacePolicyOnline, which is not an accepted publisher. The SpaceX official quoted also credited the record largely to favourable orbital timing ('We got lucky this time'). The previous day's genius story was also about SpaceX.

candidates.headline: NASA's Roman Space Telescope takes its first coronagraph observation (Goddard, MD)
candidates.reason: Only the ScienceDaily page (Oct 2) was opened. The NASA blog could not be fetched before the tool limit was reached. First light was Sept 22, before the window; NASA announced it Sept 30. It is also arguably an operational commissioning step.

candidates.headline: Illinois professor Kaiyu Guan named 2026 MacArthur Fellow
candidates.reason: Only the University of Illinois release was opened. No accepted news page could be found or opened before the tool limit was reached.

candidates.headline: UT Austin researchers re-date Oklahoma's Ames impact crater to about 370 million years ago
candidates.reason: The ScienceDaily page is dated Oct 4, after the scan date. The other coverage found was on Gizmodo, Yahoo and Starlust, none of which are accepted.

candidates.headline: Physicists identify 'octupolar' magnetism

candidates.headline: Two studies boost case that Enceladus's ocean could support life

candidates.headline: University at Buffalo study links RNA's 2'-OH group to droplet formation relevant to the origin of life

candidates.headline: MIT finds a hidden cancer risk of the keto diet; Cornell finds a human brain gene that can jump through DNA

candidates.headline: Washington State University-led modified niclosamide shows promise against endometriosis in mice

candidates.headline: Harvard-led study finds transplanted hearts adjust to the recipient's biological age
